chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:
I said to Abī 'Abd Allāh عليه السلام: A woman experiences a wet dream in sleep and emits the greater fluid. He said: Ghusl (ritual bath) is not obligatory upon her.

The correct understanding of this report is that if she sees the greater fluid during her sleep, but when she awakens she does not see anything, then ghusl is not obligatory upon her. This indicates that.

key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required after certain states of major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْمَاءَ الْأَعْظَمَ: the major emitted fluid referred to in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman addressed in the legal ruling
key_terms.تَحْتَلِمُ: experiences a sexual dream during sleep
key_terms.شَيْئًا: any actual trace or substance found upon waking

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to perform ghusl if she sees discharge in a dream but finds nothing upon waking?
ai.summary: This report addresses the fiqh ruling concerning a woman who dreams of discharge in sleep. Its stated reconciliation is that if she sees this in the dream but finds no trace upon waking, then ghusl (ritual bath) is not obligatory upon her.
